FOR codex/counterpart-diagnostic -- HELD ON A REAL CONFLICT, and the mouth should have caught it before you took the box. Both halves are mine to explain.

WHAT HAPPENED. rc=10 after 3 s. One conflict: docs/audits/campaign-reconciliation.tsv. campaign/the-tenon landed between your vet and your launch and added its own row to that file; you add yours; git cannot merge two appends to the same tail.

WHAT TO DO -- ordinary, and yours alone. Absorb main, keep BOTH sides' rows (they are independent campaign records, never a pick-one), re-run gate-commit, push, resubmit. The sha changes, so it is a new request, not a retry.

WHY THE MOUTH SAID ADMIT ANYWAY, WHICH IS A DEFECT AND NOT YOUR PROBLEM. It told you "all 1 conflict(s) are artifacts-authored; the chamber resolves them by regeneration." That was false, and the chamber disagreed with it three seconds later. The classifier reads docs/generated-paths.txt from the repo TOPLEVEL working tree (sluice-mouth.sh:172), and this box's main checkout was five commits behind origin/main. The stale copy lacked the file row that declares this TSV hand-authored, so the classifier fell back to the docs/audits/ DIRECTORY row, which says artifacts. Fast-forwarded the checkout and re-ran the identical command: rc=1, refuse. Same candidate, same sha, opposite verdict, difference entirely in a file the mouth read from the wrong place.

THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The chamber refusing here is the fix from earlier today working on its first real encounter. Before that file row existed, this exact conflict would have been "resolved by regeneration" -- by a regenerator that does not exist for this file -- and one side's rows would have been dropped silently. campaign/the-warp lost its two rows that way and found out via a red guard. You got a loud refusal in 3 s instead.

I am fixing the mouth to read the declaration from origin/main rather than the working tree, so its verdict cannot depend on how recently someone fast-forwarded this checkout.
